questions.q: What is the default sort direction of ORDER BY?
options: Ascending (ASC) — smallest to largest, or A to Z
Descending (DESC) — largest to smallest
Random
Insertion order, always
questions.explain: ASC is the default; DESC must be written explicitly to reverse it.

questions.q: In 'ORDER BY Color ASC, ListPrice DESC', what does the second column do?
options: Breaks ties within each Color group, sorting by ListPrice highest first
Overrides the Color sort entirely
Sorts the entire table by ListPrice first, ignoring Color
Causes a syntax error — only one column can be used in ORDER BY
questions.explain: Additional ORDER BY columns only matter for rows that tie on the columns before them.

questions.q: Why does this course avoid sorting by column position (e.g. ORDER BY 3)?
options: It's fragile — reordering or adding columns to the SELECT list silently changes what gets sorted
Sorting by position is not valid T-SQL syntax
It only works with numeric columns
It's slower than sorting by column name
questions.explain: Column-position sorting works, but a later edit to the SELECT list can silently break it without any error.

questions.q: Why can ORDER BY reference a SELECT alias when WHERE (Lesson 11) cannot?
options: ORDER BY is the last clause evaluated, after SELECT has already created the alias
ORDER BY and WHERE are evaluated at the exact same time
Aliases can never be used in ORDER BY either
It's a special exception with no relation to processing order
questions.explain: This ties directly back to Lesson 11's logical processing order — ORDER BY runs after SELECT, so the alias already exists by then.

questions.q: What happens if a query has no ORDER BY at all?
options: SQL Server doesn't guarantee any particular row order
Rows always come back in alphabetical order by the first column
Rows always come back in primary key order
The query fails with an error
questions.explain: Without an explicit ORDER BY, row order is whatever is convenient for the engine — not something to rely on.
